title: Android Auto, Automotive OS, and Driver Safety

scout.purpose: Master android auto, automotive os, and driver safety through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend android auto, automotive os, and driver safety.

blocks.text: Android Auto projects compatible experiences from a phone; Android Automotive OS runs applications on the vehicle platform. Supported app categories, templates, quality tiers, permissions, and distribution differ. The vehicle is not a large phone. Use the Android for Cars App Library or supported media surfaces and let the host render safety-reviewed templates. Driver distraction restrictions can change with driving state, and parked experiences must remain clearly separated.

blocks.text: Design shallow tasks, minimal choices, voice where supported, large targets, predictable back behavior, and immediate error recovery. Do not expose arbitrary Compose or WebView UI on restricted driving surfaces. Model connectivity between phone, vehicle, backend, and media session; resume after disconnect without duplicate actions. Automotive hardware and vehicle properties have privileged or OEM-specific boundaries. Never infer safety-critical state from unsupported signals or make the app authority for vehicle control.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Test Android Auto and Automotive OS separately with official hosts or emulators, day and night, rotary or touch, voice, no network, disconnect, audio focus, interruption, driver-state restrictions, and category-specific quality checks. Verify direct playback or navigation behavior where required. Privacy includes passenger or driver identity, location, voice, contacts, and vehicle data. Review release eligibility and regional rules before promising a feature.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Building a custom dense touchscreen UI for Android Automotive bypasses template and distraction constraints and may be unusable or rejected.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

recall.prompt: What is the architectural difference between Auto and Automotive OS?
recall.answer: Auto projects a phone-powered experience into the car, while Automotive OS runs apps on the vehicle platform.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
